22E.4 War as a defense from unprovoked attack.

precepts.text: Nahash the Ammonite besieged Jabesh-gilead and would make a covenant only on condition of thrusting out all their right eyes, a reproach upon all Israel.
precepts.point: Remember that the children of Ammon had been warring with Israel; they got smashed and put under tribute back in the days of Saul.

note.label: 2 Samuel 10: The Children of Ammon and the Syrians Smitten

precepts.why:
“Then Nahash the Ammonite came up, and encamped against Jabesh–gilead”. When the men of Jabesh asked him for a covenant, he answered, “On this condition will I make a covenant with you, that I may thrust out all your right eyes, and lay it for a reproach upon all Israel.”

That is the Nahash whose son Hanun now reigned over the children of Ammon. David said, “I will shew kindness unto Hanun the son of Nahash, as his father shewed kindness unto me”, and sent his servants to comfort him for his father.

Remember who the children of Ammon were. They had been warring with Israel, and they got smashed and put under tribute back in the days of Saul.

precepts.text: David had already dedicated unto the Most High the silver and gold of the nations he subdued, including Syria, Moab, and the children of Ammon.
precepts.point: Once these men saw David did not like what happened, they knew David was a man of war and Israel a people of war, so they sought help. But David had already subdued these same nations; they simply tried to get the men who had always been beefing with Israel to come against Israel yet again.

note.label: 2 Samuel 10: The Children of Ammon and the Syrians Smitten

precepts.why:
David had already dedicated unto the Lord “the silver and gold that he had dedicated of all nations which he subdued; Of Syria, and of Moab, and of the children of Ammon, and of the Philistines, and of Amalek, and of the spoil of Hadadezer, son of Rehob, king of Zobah.”

So when “the children of Ammon saw that they stank before David” and hired the Syrians of Beth-rehob and of Zoba, of king Maacah and of Ish-tob, they were calling on nations David had already subdued. Syria, Ammon, Rehob and Zobah are all in that list of the spoil.

Once they saw David did not like what happened, they knew David was a man of war and Israel a people of war, so they sought help. They simply tried to get the men who had always been beefing with Israel to come against Israel yet again.

precepts.text: They shall run like mighty men and climb the wall like men of war, every one marching in his ways without breaking ranks.
precepts.point: This is how much of a warrior nation Israel is: Joab put his troops in a battle array to fight two enemies at one time. That warrior mentality is already etched inside us; we just have to keep the commandments so it can come back out, as it is going to according to Joel 2.

note.label: 2 Samuel 10: The Children of Ammon and the Syrians Smitten

precepts.why:
“They shall run like mighty men; they shall climb the wall like men of war; and they shall march every one on his ways, and they shall not break their ranks:”

That is Joab at the gate of Ammon. With the children of Ammon in array at the entering in of the gate and the Syrians by themselves in the field, “the front of the battle was against him before and behind”. So he chose of all the choice men of Israel against the Syrians and gave the rest into the hand of Abishai his brother against Ammon: “If the Syrians be too strong for me, then thou shalt help me: but if the children of Ammon be too strong for thee, then I will come and help thee.”

This is how much of a warrior nation Israel is: Joab put his troops in a battle array to fight two enemies at one time. That warrior mentality is already etched inside us. We just have to keep the commandments so it can come back out, as it is going to according to Joel 2.

points: Remember that the children of Ammon had been warring with Israel; they got smashed and put under tribute back in the days of Saul.

note.label: 2 Samuel 10: The Children of Ammon and the Syrians Smitten

points: The king of the children of Ammon died and Hanun his son reigned in his stead. David said he would show kindness unto Hanun as his father Nahash had shown kindness unto David, and sent his servants to comfort him for his father.

note.label: 2 Samuel 10: The Children of Ammon and the Syrians Smitten

points: The princes of Ammon told their lord Hanun that David had not sent comforters to honor his father, but had rather sent his servants to search the city, to spy it out, and to overthrow it.

Through one generation to another they still had this beef with Israel; they kept it in their mind that these people were enemies, not meant to be at peace with them. So they put it in the king's mind that David was really coming to spy the land out and overthrow them.

note.label: 2 Samuel 10: The Children of Ammon and the Syrians Smitten

points: Hanun took David's servants, shaved off one half of their beards, cut off their garments in the middle even unto their buttocks, and sent them away. When it was told David, he sent to meet them because the men were greatly ashamed, telling them to tarry at Jericho until their beards be grown, then return.

One of the first things we learn coming into this truth is that a man has to have a beard and men have to pull up their pants. The beard is a badge of manly dignity, a law given by the Most High, and it is a shame for a man to shave it. These men were ashamed to come into the city with half a beard and their garments cut so their behind was showing; David did not even want them in the city until their beards grew back. That is what Israel has to change as a people; today men walk around with their behind showing as a fashion statement, but these men were greatly ashamed.

note.label: 2 Samuel 10: The Children of Ammon and the Syrians Smitten

points: When the children of Ammon saw that they stank before David, they hired the Syrians of Beth-rehob and Zoba, twenty thousand footmen, and of king Maacah a thousand men, and of Ish-tob twelve thousand men.

Once these men saw David did not like what happened, they knew David was a man of war and Israel a people of war, so they sought help. But David had already subdued these same nations; they simply tried to get the men who had always been beefing with Israel to come against Israel yet again.

note.label: 2 Samuel 10: The Children of Ammon and the Syrians Smitten

points: When David heard it he sent Joab and all the host of the mighty men. The children of Ammon put the battle in array at the gate, and the Syrians were by themselves in the field. Seeing the battle set against him before and behind, Joab chose of the choice men of Israel against the Syrians and delivered the rest into the hand of Abishai his brother against the children of Ammon, each ready to help the other if too strong.

This is how much of a warrior nation Israel is: Joab put his troops in a battle array to fight two enemies at one time. That warrior mentality is already etched inside us; we just have to keep the commandments so it can come back out, as it is going to according to Joel 2.

note.label: 2 Samuel 10: The Children of Ammon and the Syrians Smitten

points: Joab charged them to be of good courage and play the men for their people and the cities of their God. When Joab and his men drew nigh, the Syrians fled before him, and when the children of Ammon saw the Syrians flee, they also fled before Abishai and entered into the city, and Joab returned to Jerusalem.

note.label: 2 Samuel 10: The Children of Ammon and the Syrians Smitten

points: When the Syrians saw they were smitten before Israel, they gathered together, and Hadarezer sent for the Syrians beyond the river with Shobach the captain of the host. David gathered all Israel, passed over Jordan, and the Syrians fled before Israel. David slew the men of seven hundred chariots and forty thousand horsemen and smote Shobach, who died there.

note.label: 2 Samuel 10: The Children of Ammon and the Syrians Smitten

points: When all the kings that were servants to Hadarezer saw they were smitten before Israel, they made peace and served them, and the Syrians feared to help the children of Ammon anymore. This is what happens when you mess with the armies of the living God: they got whooped so badly that the Syrians would not even help the Ammonites anymore.
